claims.title: righteousness is thicker than compliance and narrower than the whole good
claims.summary: Righteousness should be treated as a distinct moral concept rather than collapsed into legality, piety, or generic goodness.

claims.title: cross-tradition recurrences justify a shared research program
claims.summary: Despite major differences, Greek, biblical, Islamic, Confucian, Thomist, and modern secular materials recur around due-ness, pressure, vulnerable parties, and public order.

claims.title: narrow-waist theory of righteousness
claims.summary: Righteousness is steadfast practical fidelity to valid claims, right order, and breach-responsive repair across relations, roles, and institutions, especially under pressure.

claims.title: righteousness is pressure-tested
claims.summary: Serious accounts of righteousness become most visible when profit, fear, office, ritual substitution, or status tempt agents away from what is due.

claims.title: repair is breach-responsive and becomes constitutive once wrong is in view
claims.summary: Righteousness is not always already reparative, but after breach, wrongful benefit, or damaged standing it requires acknowledgment, responsibility uptake, and reparative action rather than clean-hands distance or symbolic closure.

claims.title: righteousness is relation-first, person-carried, and institution-shaped
claims.summary: Relations and claim-structures explain what is due; persons are the primary accountable bearers of answerability; institutions shape whether right response is supported or corrupted at scale.

claims.title: righteous office is entrusted power kept publicly answerable and anti-captured
claims.summary: Public office is not just private decency in a role; it is a role-specific burden to use entrusted power on publicly justifiable terms, resist capture, and preserve correction and repair.

claims.title: righteousness has a portable core and tradition-thick forms
claims.summary: Comparative work should distinguish the recurrent structure of claim-answerability under pressure from thicker traditions that ground righteousness in God, covenant, sacred order, or other larger moral frames.

claims.title: portable claims require typed recognition and public-translation status
claims.summary: Comparative portability claims should distinguish recognition status (identity, incomplete identity, analogue, rejection) from whether a translated form is being offered as a publicly shareable module for common institutions.

claims.title: righteousness occupies a threshold-band above bare nonwrongdoing and below universal heroism
claims.summary: Righteousness requires active due-fidelity under pressure and is disqualified by capture, laundering, and repair refusal, but it does not require every supererogatory sacrifice that would count as heroic or saintly.

claims.title: righteous repair does not require victim forgiveness or restored intimacy
claims.summary: After breach, a response may count as righteous through acknowledgment, reparative action, and non-recurrence even when forgiveness is not given and close relationship is not restored.

claims.title: righteousness claims are standing-sensitive and can be presumptively defeated
claims.summary: Capture, hypocritical self-exemption, laundering, and unowned dirty-hands necessity do not merely count against righteousness; they presumptively defeat the claim unless the defect itself is confronted.

claims.title: some standing-defeaters are answerable only through avowal, interruption, repair, and time
claims.summary: A defeated righteousness claim may sometimes be followed by a righteous response and later partial requalification, but later confession or apology cannot retroactively purify the tainted act itself.

claims.title: public righteousness claims require contestability, and secrecy raises rather than cancels the justificatory burden
claims.summary: Private righteousness may remain partly hidden, but offices and institutions cannot rely on self-certifying virtue; serious public righteousness claims require publicly offerable reasons, preserved record, review-capable process, and stronger substitute safeguards where secrecy blocks ordinary transparency.

claims.title: righteousness under conflict requires disciplined priority and honest carriage of remainder
claims.summary: When valid claims collide, righteousness does not require satisfying every due at once; it requires truthful triage using morally serious priority cues while acknowledging unsatisfied remainder and any later burdens of explanation, mitigation, or repair.

claims.title: righteousness verdicts should distinguish episode, standing, and trajectory
claims.summary: A single act may be righteous without establishing settled righteous standing; damaged standing may improve through avowal, repair, competent repeat performance, and time without retroactively purifying the earlier tainted act.

claims.title: righteousness under uncertainty requires inquiry, fair testimony uptake, and revisable action
claims.summary: When facts or moral application remain materially uncertain, righteousness requires proportionate inquiry, fair uptake of testimony, explicit acknowledgment of uncertainty, and actions designed to remain reviewable, revisable, reversible, or repairable as evidence improves.

claims.title: delegation may distribute labor without delegating away righteous standing
claims.summary: Delegated action may be necessary and legitimate, but claim-setting, guardrails, contestability, and repair ownership remain at least partly nondelegable; many-hands complexity is a tracing problem, not a solvent of answerability.

claims.title: righteous conflict-judgment is guided by portable priority cues and fair burden placement
claims.summary: When valid claims collide, righteousness is not neutral balancing among all interests; serious harm, urgent need, dependency, induced reliance, creator-burden, and reversibility normally matter more than gain, convenience, status, or image, and the more powerful or burden-creating side should ordinarily absorb more of the remainder.

claims.title: righteous judgment may correct rule underfit through equity without licensing favoritist exception
claims.summary: Righteousness normally prefers public, general, and reviewable rules, but because rules are general and cases particular it sometimes requires equitable correction. Such correction is righteous only when tied to the rule's point, responsive to morally relevant differences, publicly articulable, consistent across like cases, and preserved in record or review rather than hidden as insider privilege.

claims.title: righteousness may require interruption rather than compliant participation in compromised roles
claims.summary: When continued participation would materially launder abuse, false standing, or blocked answerability, righteousness may require objection, recusal, protected disclosure, resignation, or burdened public witness rather than obedient role-fidelity. Such interruption is righteous only when aimed at due-facing correction, disciplined by truth and evidence, proportionate to the wrong, and answerable for its own remainder.

claims.title: righteous sanction rejects both cruelty theater and favoritist mercy laundering
claims.summary: When wrong has been named and sanction is in view, righteousness neither equates severity with moral seriousness nor treats leniency as automatically humane. Righteous sanction names the wrong, protects against recurrence, and keeps repair in view; righteous mercy is authority-side restraint that cannot be bought by victim pressure, selective indulgence, or hidden impunity.

claims.title: public office is held in trust rather than owned, and fiduciary language works as a qualified sharpening cue
claims.summary: The archive now treats office powers, information, secrecy, discretion, and opportunities as held public powers rather than personal or factional property. A qualified fiduciary cue sharpens loyalty, care, deliberation, impartiality, accountability, and anti-appropriation, while the archive stops short of saying every public role is literally identical to a private-law fiduciary relation.

claims.title: good ends do not by themselves make an exercise of public power righteous if the wrong bearer, inadequate competence, or missing authorization is doing the work
claims.summary: Righteous office is bearer-disciplined as well as due-facing. Public acts that burden, permit, or coerce must be carried by the right bearer, with adequate competence and real authorization; otherwise the better verdict is often standing-defective office usurpation, or else a different type such as interruption or witness rather than righteous office-performance.

claims.title: public righteousness materially burdening others is presumptively defective if it rules over their heads instead of making them present through hearing, accountable representation, or a justified substitute
claims.summary: For public decisions that materially burden identifiable people or communities, righteousness requires more than public reasons and later review. It normally requires some domain-fit way of making the burdened present in judgment — direct hearing, meaningful participation, accountable representation, or, where urgency, scale, or incapacity blocks those, a substitute that remains open to later challenge and repair.

claims.title: when claimants cannot directly appear, righteousness requires support-before-substitution, accountable proxy voice, and stewardship rather than treating absence as no claim
claims.summary: The archive now treats absent claimants as morally present when burdens fall on children, persons needing supported agency, diffuse publics, or future persons. It prefers direct supported agency where possible, conflict-screened proxy voice where necessary, and stewardship rather than self-authorized ventriloquism where no present speaker can fully stand in for those burdened.

claims.title: special ties may thicken what is due, but they do not erase baseline due and in impartial public office they often trigger restraint rather than privileged service
claims.summary: The archive now rejects both flat impartiality and unrestricted loyalty. Family, friendship, promise, dependency, and entrusted representation can intensify obligation, but these ties remain bounded by baseline due to outsiders; in adjudicative, allocative, or disciplinary public roles, private ties commonly require recusal, anti-preferential-treatment discipline, or anti-nepotism restraint instead of favored service.

claims.title: righteousness is not reducible to non-domination, but benevolent mastery is not enough where one side remains subject to uncontrolled power
claims.summary: The archive now treats anti-domination as a sharpening rule rather than a total reduction. A relation may look humane in episodes yet remain unrighteous if the weaker party still lives at another's mercy under discretionary control, retaliation risk, blocked exit, or favor-dependent security.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened not only by lying but also by misleading and manipulative management of others' reliance
claims.summary: The archive now treats candor as standing-relevant. A claim to righteousness can fail not only through direct falsehood but through selective truth, euphemistic misdirection, manipulative framing, or false reassurance that gets others to trust, comply, forgive, or stand down on a basis the speaker cannot honestly avow.

claims.title: promises, oaths, assurances, and office undertakings can thicken what is due, but wrongful or unauthorized undertakings do not become righteous merely by being kept
claims.summary: The archive now treats keeping faith as a real burden of righteousness because promise-like undertakings voluntarily invite reliance and create more determinate claims. But fidelity is not idolatry: a corrupt, discriminatory, or authority-exceeding undertaking does not become righteous through literal performance, and when such an undertaking must break the remaining burdens run through avowal, release-seeking where possible, mitigation, and repair.

claims.title: gratitude for benefaction can be fitting, but gifts and favors do not buy silence, deference, or preferential treatment, especially in public office
claims.summary: The archive now treats benefaction as morally real without letting it become a solvent of judgment. Gifts, rescue, hospitality, sponsorship, and other favors may call for thanks or goodwill, but they do not create a standing right to later compliance, access, or favoritist treatment; in office they are burdened because they can privatize entrusted power or generate dependence.

claims.title: formal consent or mutual advantage do not by themselves make an arrangement righteous when gain is extracted from vulnerability or constrained refusal
claims.summary: The archive now treats exploitation as a standing-relevant defect. A signature, waiver, price, or desperate yes can still express agency while failing to legitimate the arrangement morally when the stronger party is relying on desperation, dependence, ignorance, or badly constrained options rather than fair terms, real understanding, and meaningful refusal.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened not only by direct wrongdoing but also by knowingly enabling, benefiting from, or laundering others' wrongdoing where resistance is due
claims.summary: The archive now treats complicity as a standing-relevant burden rather than a mere edge case. Distance from the first wrong can change degree and remedy, but it does not automatically erase involvement where an actor is supplying practical help, legitimization, institutional shelter, retained gain, or continued participation after the connection to wrongdoing becomes visible.

claims.title: guilt, punishment, and civic disability do not travel by bloodline, shared label, or mere association, though real group authorship and knowing participation still matter
claims.summary: The archive now rejects collective punishment, corruption of blood, and guilt by mere association. Kinship, demographic overlap, constituency relation, or organizational nearness do not by themselves carry blame or penalty; but righteousness also rejects fake moral atomism, so coordinated group authorship, office responsibility, and knowing participation still generate burdens that must be traced rather than smeared or denied.

claims.title: even where sanction, custody, or public censure is due, righteousness is burdened by humiliation, degrading treatment, and abasement spectacle
claims.summary: The archive now treats nonabasement as a standing-relevant limit on righteous discipline. Punishment, confinement, exposure, removal, and truthful censure may be due, but once contempt, humiliative spectacle, ritualized inferiority, or degrading treatment is doing the real work, righteousness is collapsing into domination, audience management, or status destruction rather than accountable protection and truth.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when a norm is applied selectively downward or outward while self and allies are indulgently exempted without a publicly relevant reason
claims.summary: The archive now treats reciprocal and like-cases testing as a sharper discipline on hypocritical self-exemption. Not every asymmetry is hypocrisy: some roles, vulnerabilities, and remedial positions justify heavier or different burdens. But status, affinity, side, and convenience do not by themselves justify one law for others and another for self.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when an accuser or office materially engineers the very breach later cited as proof of guilt, danger, or unfitness
claims.summary: The archive now treats manufactured guilt as a standing-relevant defect. A later act by the target does not by itself purify the stronger party when the stronger party baited, pressured, cultivated, or strategically provoked the very failure later used to justify punishment, exclusion, or moral superiority; mere opportunity is not the same as authored breach.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when a formally valid reason, process, or category is used as pretextual cover for a reason that cannot be openly owned
claims.summary: The archive now treats pretext as a standing-relevant defect. A decision is not made righteous merely because some lawful or procedurally available rationale could have supported it; where the offered explanation is contrived, selectively invoked, or not the reason actually doing the work, formal compliance becomes form-laundering rather than genuine justification.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when complaint, testimony, disclosure, refusal, or cooperation with review is punished, chilled, or strategically burdened
claims.summary: The archive now treats reprisal as a standing-relevant defect rather than a side issue of management or civility. Protected voice does not become automatically correct, but power may not answer complaint by raising the price of speaking through threat, exclusion, scrutiny, demotion, smear, or other chilling burdens that attack answerability itself.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when serious blame or penalty runs through hidden, retroactive, or unduly vague norms
claims.summary: The archive now treats fair notice, prospectivity, and sufficient clarity as standing-relevant rather than merely technical legal values. A decision is not made righteous just because an authority can cite a rule after the fact; where the operative standard was secret, retroactively sharpened, or too vague to steer by, the burdened party is being governed by trapdoor norms rather than cleanly addressed agency.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when delay, repeated procedural friction, or exhausting waiting turn valid claims into abandonment or stale relief
claims.summary: The archive now treats delay and procedural exhaustion as standing-relevant rather than administratively incidental. A process does not stay righteous merely by remaining formally open if time, repetition, and uncertainty are doing the real work of denial, coercion, or claimant exhaustion.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when one person's body, liberty, or protected presence is used as leverage, bargaining chip, or shield to move another person's will
claims.summary: The archive now treats innocent leverage as a standing-relevant defect rather than merely hard strategy. A person may not be cleanly burdened, detained, exposed, or instrumentalized mainly so that someone else will surrender, cooperate, confess, stay quiet, or hold back.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when records, evidence, or witness channels are destroyed, suppressed, corrupted, or kept off the books so that later challenge cannot fairly proceed
claims.summary: The archive now treats cover-up and answerability sabotage as standing-relevant defects rather than mere side misconduct. Once challenge, investigation, or grave-harm inquiry is live or reasonably foreseeable, actors and offices owe preserved record, protected evidence paths, and witness channels not strategically bent toward forgetfulness.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when confession, apology, or recantation is extracted by custody, threat, dependency, or humiliative scripting and then treated as clean proof or restored standing
claims.summary: The archive now treats compelled confession and scripted avowal as standing-relevant defects. Truthful self-implication can matter for repair and requalification, but once the stronger party materially authors the admission through coercion, custodial asymmetry, or dependency pressure, the statement becomes burdened evidence and cannot by itself launder the institution or purify the actor.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when office, education, work, safety, or civic standing is conditioned on compelled creed, loyalty profession, or orthodoxy signaling beyond what truthful role performance requires
claims.summary: The archive now treats compelled creed and loyalty tests as standing-relevant defects. Offices and institutions may sometimes require support for lawful duty, constitutional order, confidentiality, or bounded factual disclosure, but they lose standing when they demand ideological profession, religious test, factional devotion, or ritual assent as the price of ordinary belonging or trust.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when work, service, or continued role-performance is held in place by menace, debt, document control, wage withholding, status dependence, or other conditions that make exit unreal
claims.summary: The archive now treats forced labour, captive service, and exit barriers as standing-relevant defects. Past agreement, migration status, prison status, or nominal resignability do not by themselves launder service into righteousness once blocked exit or menace is doing the real work of keeping the person in place.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when people are judged, excluded, silenced, or penalized for failing to clear barriers the stronger party could reasonably remove, modify, or route around
claims.summary: The archive now treats denial of needed accommodation and inaccessible compliance as standing-relevant defects. Identical treatment does not by itself settle righteousness where communication, hearing, work, study, waiting, testimony, or claim-making are blocked by channels the stronger party controls.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when the accuser, beneficiary, or implicated office also controls the verdict or appeal without real recusal, structural separation, or independent review
claims.summary: The archive now treats interested adjudication and self-review as standing-relevant defects. Actual sincerity is not enough when the forum is designed so that accusation, institutional stake, and decision collapse together.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when a person, office, or institution demands or preserves more personal legibility than the task, risk, or due can justify
claims.summary: The archive now treats arbitrary intrusion, excessive surveillance, overbroad search, intimate exposure, and indefinite retention as standing-relevant defects. Accountable institutions need enough proof to answer for what they do, but not unlimited visibility into the people under their power.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when emergency or necessity is used to create a self-justifying zone of exception
claims.summary: The archive now treats emergency rhetoric, indefinite derogation, and crisis-based self-expansion as standing-relevant defects. Genuine emergencies may justify temporary extraordinary measures, but only under strict necessity, narrow scope, sunset, review, and visible return-to-normalcy burdens.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when persons or peoples are left without reasonable access to the essentials of a minimally decent life
claims.summary: The archive now treats food, water, basic shelter or housing, and essential care as floor claims that may require fair triage under scarcity but may not be handled through favoritism, hidden ranking, or normalized abandonment. Righteous action protects the floor first by public reasons and remains answerable for any unmet remainder.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when power solves conflict, danger, or administrative inconvenience by uprooting people
claims.summary: The archive now treats displacement, collective expulsion, forced eviction, blocked return, and cleansing-style population management as standing-relevant defects. Even justified evacuation or relocation requires explored alternatives, individualized or minimally indiscriminate judgment, dignified conditions, and a real path toward return, restitution, or non-degrading resettlement rather than warehousing or disappearance.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when power governs through collective punishment or civilian deprivation
claims.summary: The archive now treats collective punishment, starvation-style pressure, blocked relief, and other forms of indiscriminate deprivation as standing-relevant defects. Broad restrictions may sometimes be protective, but righteousness is usually defeated once area-wide suffering becomes the method for punishing, coercing, or pressuring persons within the group.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when power separates families, blocks contact, or frustrates reunification mainly to punish, deter, or simplify control
claims.summary: The archive now treats family fracture as a standing-relevant defect. Separation may sometimes be justified for a child's safety or other concrete protective reasons, but once power causes the separation it carries live duties of notice, contact, whereabouts, and humane reunion rather than discretionary grace.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when essential care is denied, delayed, obstructed, or politically sorted, or when healers are turned into instruments of coercion
claims.summary: The archive now treats punitive noncare, discriminatory treatment access, obstruction of care delivery, and coercive capture of medical work as standing-relevant defects. Triage, quarantine, and emergency scarcity may justify narrower limits, but only if they remain medically grounded, non-discriminatory, minimally punitive, and reviewable rather than using untreated suffering as leverage.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when legal existence, ordinary services, or family continuity are made to depend on papers people cannot safely get, keep, or correct
claims.summary: The archive now treats rightlessness-by-paper as a standing-relevant defect. Identity assurance and civil registration may be necessary, but documentation systems become unrighteous when discriminatory design, confiscation, mismatch, excessive proof demands, or privacy-destructive digital gates make persons effectively invisible to law, services, or reunion.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when power makes a person legally unfindable through secret custody, concealed transfer, false records, or blocked locating channels
claims.summary: The archive now treats enforced disappearance and disappearance-like custody as standing-relevant defects. Limited confidentiality may sometimes be justified, but not secret detention, unrecorded transfer, falsified registers, or any arrangement that places a person outside the protection of law.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when power uses pain, terror, or other cruel treatment as a method of control, confession, punishment, intimidation, or will-breaking
claims.summary: The archive now treats torture, cruel or degrading treatment, and pain-as-governance as standing-relevant defects. Necessary restraint may sometimes be justified for immediate protection, but emergency, superior order, and mere noncompliance do not purify practices that make suffering itself the instrument; righteous order also carries burdens of inspection, complaint, investigation, exclusion of torture-tainted proof, and repair.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when power deprives people of liberty without a clear, necessary, and reviewable basis, or treats detention as the easy answer
claims.summary: The archive now treats arbitrary detention, pretrial custody-by-default, and prolonged administrative confinement as standing-relevant defects. Liberty burdens do not disappear because detention carries a formal label; righteousness requires prompt reasons, prompt review, meaningful challenge, serious consideration of narrower alternatives, and repair where custody was unlawful or unnecessary.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when power takes life without strict necessity, or makes killing easier than capture, care, delay, or de-escalation
claims.summary: The archive now treats arbitrary killing, lethal-force-by-convenience, and preventable death under public power as standing-relevant defects. In law-enforcement and custody settings, lethal force remains exceptional and tightly necessity-bound; across domains, potentially unlawful death triggers preservation, investigation, and truth duties rather than euphemism or institutional self-cleansing.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when serious judgment is imposed through a process the burdened person cannot meaningfully understand, answer, test, or appeal
claims.summary: The archive now treats fair trial, practical defense, and no-conviction-by-opacity as standing-relevant. A hearing on paper is not enough; serious adjudication requires competent and impartial forum, intelligible notice, usable counsel where needed, meaningful chance to test adverse proof and present defense, and review strong enough that secrecy, foregone outcome, or convenience do not become the hidden authors of judgment.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when power removes, rejects, extradites, or transfers a person by exporting them into persecution, torture, disappearance, or other irreparable harm
claims.summary: The archive now treats non-refoulement and no-risk-export as standing-relevant. Removal may sometimes be justified, but not through pushback, frontier rejection, third-country routing, or diplomatic-assurance design that denies a person individualized protection assessment or hands them into foreseeable grave danger.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when power denies, strips, or conditions nationality in ways that arbitrarily or discriminatorily create statelessness, civic unreality, or exile by paper
claims.summary: The archive now treats nationality, statelessness, and no-exile-by-paper as standing-relevant. States may regulate membership, but not by making belonging hostage to impossible proof, discriminatory transmission rules, security theater, or denationalization practices that render a person stateless, removable, or civically unreal while practical standing collapses.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when power suppresses peaceful assembly mainly to avoid criticism, erase visibility, or simplify control
claims.summary: The archive now treats peaceful assembly, protest, and no-order-by-suppression as standing-relevant. Public order may justify narrow lawful limits, but non-violent assemblies remain protected even when spontaneous, unauthorized, or disruptive; authorities owe facilitation and differentiated protection duties, and force or dispersal must remain exceptional, minimized, and answerable.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when power silences criticism, reporting, or access to public-interest information mainly to avoid scrutiny or monopolize narrative
claims.summary: The archive now treats freedom of expression, press, and no-silencing-by-power as standing-relevant. Opinion may not be interfered with, expression includes seeking, receiving, and imparting information, and narrow lawful restrictions remain possible only under steep burdens of legality, necessity, proportionality, public-information access, and protection for journalists and other vulnerable speakers.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when power makes collective organization contingent on prior indulgence, capture, or retaliatory risk
claims.summary: The archive now treats freedom of association, unions, and no-association-by-sufferance as standing-relevant. People may be regulated narrowly for real protective reasons, but they may not be left to organize only through selective permission, employer domination, anti-union discrimination, or other systems that make independent collective life practically unavailable.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when power excludes citizens from public affairs through unreasonable voting barriers, sham electoral design, intimidation, discriminatory candidacy rules, or unequal access to public service
claims.summary: The archive now treats political participation, elections, and no-rule-by-exclusion as standing-relevant. Participation must be genuinely usable rather than ceremonial: citizens must be able to vote, stand, influence public affairs, and reach public service on equal terms without unreasonable barriers, fear, or managed inclusion that preserves consent-talk while narrowing who can count in practice.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when power coerces belief, punishes conversion or nonbelief, suppresses worship or observance beyond narrow necessity, or distributes ordinary standing through favored orthodoxy
claims.summary: The archive now treats freedom of thought, conscience, religion, and no-orthodoxy-by-power as standing-relevant. The inward forum is not public property: freedom to have or adopt a religion or belief is not subject to limitation, manifestations may be limited only under steep burdens, and religion-or-belief discrimination or selective permission makes plural belonging practically unreal even when formal liberty remains on paper.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when power traps people in place, withholds practical exit, or arbitrarily denies return
claims.summary: The archive now treats freedom of movement, residence, return, and no-confinement-by-closure as standing-relevant. Protective limits can exist, but offices may not solve danger, dissent, demographic preference, or administrative inconvenience by governing through closure, encampment, passport denial, permit grids, or indefinite no-return.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when law, office, or institutions rank ordinary standing by protected status or status-proxy
claims.summary: The archive now treats equality, non-discrimination, and no-status-ranked standing as standing-relevant. Equal wording is not enough where protected status or facially neutral design keeps doing hierarchy work in practice; reasonable accommodation, effect-sensitive review, and temporary corrective measures may be part of equality rather than deviations from it.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when child-facing authority treats custody as title rather than stewardship
claims.summary: The archive now treats child standing, evolving capacities, and no-custody-as-title as standing-relevant. Parents, schools, welfare systems, and custodians may guide and protect, but they may not convert dependence into ownership, silence, deterrent leverage, ideological capture, or permanent tutelage; best interests, heard views, family relation, and developmental widening of agency remain live burdens.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when home and housing security are governed through clearance, serial eviction, or revocable mercy rather than secure standing
claims.summary: The archive now treats housing security, tenure, and no-homelessness-by-clearance as standing-relevant. Adequate housing is not exhausted by a bed for the night; security of tenure, affordability, habitability, services, and a credible path away from repeated clearance or emergency warehousing matter, and eviction or public-space removal cannot be laundered into righteousness by tidiness, image, or routine property administration alone.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when subsistence support is governed through punitive conditionality, opaque suspicion, or destitution-capable sanction rather than secure social standing
claims.summary: The archive now treats social security, welfare administration, and no-destitution-by-sanction as standing-relevant. Social security is not mere emergency charity: availability, adequacy, accessibility, reviewability, and dignity matter, and welfare systems become unrighteous when support for basic living is structured mainly to punish, deter, surveil, or thin claimant populations by making subsistence depend on precarity.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when education is governed through exclusion, segregation, inaccessible design, or coerced conformity rather than equal and inclusive standing
claims.summary: The archive now treats education, schooling, and no-schooling-by-exclusion as standing-relevant. Education is not merely seat placement or credential throughput: availability, accessibility, acceptability, adaptability, non-discrimination, and inclusive design matter, and school systems become unrighteous when learning and future standing are allocated by exclusion, segregation, unaffordable barriers, documentary precarity, degrading removal, or ideological capture.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when access to livelihood depends on dangerous, degrading, discriminatorily closed, union-broken, inaccessible, or practically unleaveable work
claims.summary: The archive now treats work, livelihood, and no-livelihood-by-domination as standing-relevant. Work is not exhausted by possession of a job: access to livelihood must remain meaningfully choosable and leavable, under just and favourable conditions with fair remuneration, safety, equal standing, and real room for worker voice and organization rather than dependence on domination through labour.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when liberty, welfare, work, schooling, housing, movement, safety, or public voice are substantially governed through opaque, unchallengeable, proxy-discriminatory, surveillance-hungry, or vendor-laundered automated systems
claims.summary: The archive now treats algorithmic governance, automated decision-making, and no-rightlessness-by-model as standing-relevant. Automated systems may assist bounded judgment, but only where risk assessment, transparency, human oversight, privacy discipline, contestability, and remedy remain real and where a human bearer still owns reasons, override power, and repair rather than hiding behind models or vendors.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when support, guardianship, or incapacity law makes a person live in civic life mainly through somebody else's will
claims.summary: The archive now treats legal capacity, supported decision-making, and no-civil-death-by-guardianship as standing-relevant. Support for decision-making may be necessary and often righteous, but it must preserve the person's own authority rather than reallocating personhood through guardianship, substituted judgment, incapacity scripts, or managed signatures that thin rights, remedy, and participation across civic life.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when safe water, sanitation, hygiene, or wastewater protection are governed through shutoff, unaffordability, contamination, inaccessible design, or degrading dependence
claims.summary: The archive now treats water, sanitation, and no-thirst-by-administration as standing-relevant. Water and sanitation are dignity-bearing floor conditions rather than ordinary utilities: regulation, scarcity response, and pricing may exist, but they must preserve safety, accessibility, affordability, privacy, and hardship protection rather than making exposed people carry infrastructural failure through thirst, unsafe sanitation, or humiliating dependence.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when adequate food is governed through unaffordability, punitive administration, opaque eligibility, concentrated food-system power, or discretionary feeding mercy
claims.summary: The archive now treats food, nutrition, and no-hunger-by-administration as standing-relevant. Food is not merely a commodity flow or charitable remainder: scarcity management, pricing, and rationing may exist, but they must preserve adequate nourishment, affordability, non-discrimination, and urgent remedy rather than making exposed people carry fiscal strain, concentrated market power, or administrative indifference through hunger and malnutrition.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when clean air, non-toxic living conditions, and freedom from hazardous exposure are governed through sacrifice-zone design, dirty infrastructure, weak enforcement, or cleanup delay
claims.summary: Environmental governance is standing-defective when it predictably makes some people live, work, learn, or dwell through hazardous exposure mainly to externalize costs, simplify planning, or preserve politically convenient contamination.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when budgets, debt service, fiscal consolidation, or public-finance design make basic rights effectively conditional on fiscal tidiness
claims.summary: Public finance is not a neutral background condition. Fiscal governance is standing-defective when food, housing, care, schooling, water, environmental safety, or social protection are thinned mainly to preserve creditor confidence, politically convenient under-collection, or cleaner fiscal presentation rather than to protect rights-bearing floors under equal concern.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when rights are recognized only in forms that cannot be timely claimed, heard, or repaired
claims.summary: Rights do not become righteous by formal recognition alone. Governance is standing-defective when complaint, review, or remedy routes are too delayed, inaccessible, retaliatory, powerless, or exhausting to use before decisive harm hardens.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when land, territory, tenure, or return are governed as if only the administratively preferred title or registry could create standing
claims.summary: Land governance is standing-defective when maps, titles, inheritance scripts, acquisition law, concession design, or territorial registration make home, livelihood, culture, survival, or return depend mainly on whether customary, informal, collective, ancestral, or gender-equal claims fit the dominant property script.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when bodily and reproductive life are governed through permission, punishment, or substitute judgment rather than through the standing of the person whose body bears the consequence
claims.summary: Bodily governance is standing-defective when pregnancy, contraception, abortion, sterilization, fertility, or intimate treatment decisions turn mainly on criminal threat, third-party authorization, coerced intervention, or managed incapacity rather than on informed, noncoerced, and equal-standing agency with support where needed.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when public belonging is made effectively conditional on cultural disappearance, language abandonment, or one-way assimilation to the dominant script
claims.summary: Cultural governance is standing-defective when schooling, services, work, documentation, or civic participation become fully usable mainly for those willing to privatize, subordinate, or practically abandon their own language, cultural continuity, naming, or collective intelligibility.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when public power, service, or protection becomes informally saleable through bribery, patronage, or bought discretion
claims.summary: Office is standing-defective when permits, hiring, procurement, adjudication, welfare, care, schooling, policing, or ordinary safety become materially better, faster, or safer for those who can bribe, sponsor, privately access, or otherwise transact with decision-makers rather than rely on transparent and reviewable public criteria.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when states or lead enterprises treat privatization, contracting, or supply-chain distance as if it dissolved rights-bearing duties
claims.summary: Outsourced governance is standing-defective when essential services, coercive functions, or other rights-bearing conditions are arranged through contractors, concessionaires, platforms, landlords, utilities, or supply chains in ways that diffuse oversight and remedy while leaving affected people to absorb the burden.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when support need is governed through institutionalization, segregation, or dependency-structured living arrangements that thin self-direction and community inclusion
claims.summary: Support is standing-defective when disability, age, psychosocial difference, or crisis is answered mainly by imposed living arrangements, provider control, or blocked exit because community support was not made real. Care does not become righteous merely because services exist if those services require a person to live under other people's standing.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when ordinary standing is made to depend on connection that can be cut, throttled, or priced beyond reach
claims.summary: Disconnection is standing-defective when speech, schooling, work, welfare access, family contact, emergency information, complaint, or political participation depend on politically permitted or materially privileged connectivity, especially where digital-only design lacks affordable and realistic alternatives.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when psychosocial crisis or perceived dangerousness is governed through psychiatric coercion rather than consent-governed support
claims.summary: Care is standing-defective when mental distress, psychosocial disability, suicidality, or perceived dangerousness is answered mainly through involuntary hospitalization, forced treatment, seclusion, restraint, or other coercive control because communication, community alternatives, and consent-governed supports were not made real.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when intimate or household power thins standing through violence or coercive control while institutions treat the pattern as private life
claims.summary: Domestic governance is standing-defective when a person's safety, sexuality, credibility, income, child contact, or exit become governed through assault, coercive control, stalking, economic abuse, or post-separation process manipulation while police, courts, welfare offices, schools, or communities privatize or mutualize the pattern instead of interrupting it.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when substance use or dependency is governed through punishment or coerced abstinence rather than voluntary harm-reducing support
claims.summary: Drug policy is standing-defective when institutions respond to use, withdrawal, overdose risk, or dependency mainly through arrest, compulsory treatment, forced abstinence, naloxone or syringe denial, shelter exclusion, or similar punitive control because voluntary care, housing, and life-preserving support were not made real.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when trafficking is answered through detention, prosecution, deportation, or compelled cooperation rather than rights-preserving protection
claims.summary: Anti-trafficking governance is standing-defective when institutions respond to trafficked persons or people at serious trafficking risk mainly through arrest, immigration detention, closed shelters, prosecution for trafficking-linked conduct, visa cancellation, or similar custody-preserving control because non-punishment, safe status, survivor-directed support, and real exit from exploiters were not made primary.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when imprisonment is administered through degrading conditions rather than humane deprivation of liberty
claims.summary: Penal custody is standing-defective when prisons or jails make the sentence work mainly through overcrowding, unsafe or filthy conditions, prolonged isolation, blocked family contact, untreated illness, or emergency abandonment instead of through humane, reviewable, and reintegration-oriented confinement.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when pretrial liberty is distributed by wealth or unreachable conditions rather than individualized necessity
claims.summary: Pretrial release and bail are standing-defective when liberty before trial depends mainly on money, fixed housing, sureties, lawyer access, or technically breachable conditions that poorer and more precarious people cannot realistically satisfy instead of on individualized necessity and materially reachable alternatives.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when community supervision works mainly through tethered control rather than least-restrictive reintegration
claims.summary: Probation, parole, electronic monitoring, and related non-custodial measures are standing-defective when they make community life depend mainly on surveillance, uniform and technically breachable conditions, or easy return-to-custody instead of on individualized review, material support, and genuinely less restrictive reintegration.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when fines and fees make poverty itself into a punishment multiplier
claims.summary: Monetary sanctions are standing-defective when fixed fines, fees, or non-payment enforcement make poor people bear heavier punishment through debt, arrest exposure, or imprisonment instead of through proportionate, means-sensitive, and reviewable accountability.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when criminal records make sentence residue continue punishment after sentence completion
claims.summary: Criminal records and collateral consequences are standing-defective when open record access, disclosure, or automatic exclusions continue punishment by blocking work, housing, benefits, education, or civic standing after sentence completion instead of serving narrow, time-bounded, and reviewable protective purposes.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when property deprivation does punitive, coercive, or revenue work without rights-disciplined proof and challenge
claims.summary: Asset seizure, forfeiture, confiscation, and document-taking are standing-defective when property loss does the real work of punishment, coercion, or agency self-funding through weak proof, thin contestability, or third-party spillover rather than through narrow and reviewable recovery of genuinely illicit or danger-linked property.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when search uses bodily intrusion or exposure as a mode of control
claims.summary: Frisking, strip search, body-cavity search, scan-based screening, and repeated bodily inspection are standing-defective when exposure, humiliation, or compelled bodily legibility does the real work of security, discipline, or intimidation instead of serving a specific, least-intrusive, privacy-preserving, and reviewable need.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when biometric or genetic extraction becomes the ordinary key to access, suspicion, or public recognizability
claims.summary: Biometric and genetic systems are standing-defective when face, fingerprint, iris, voice, gait, DNA, or other extraction makes bodily or genomic extractability do the real work of verification, suspicion management, or public-space legibility instead of serving a narrow, contestable, retention-disciplined, and non-discriminatory task.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when public power initiates scrutiny mainly through category-membership or its proxies
claims.summary: Policing, border, and security systems are standing-defective when race, ethnicity, religion, nationality, migration status, perceived foreignness, neighbourhood, or proxy variables do the real work of deciding who gets stopped, checked, searched, questioned, raided, or tracked instead of individualized and conduct-linked grounds.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when list-based designation quietly does the work of exclusion, sanction, or suspicion
claims.summary: Watchlists, no-fly systems, sanctions designations, proscription registers, and similar list-based systems are standing-defective when opaque or weakly contestable inclusion does the real work of restricting movement, access, association, property, or scrutiny instead of individualized, reviewable, time-bounded, and effectively challengeable designation.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when official permission quietly becomes the source of a right
claims.summary: Permit, license, prior-authorization, and registration systems are standing-defective when official approval does the real work of deciding whether people may assemble, organize, or otherwise exercise standing-bearing freedoms instead of serving a narrow, facilitative, reviewable, and non-discriminatory administrative function.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when stigmatizing civic labels do the real work of disabling association
claims.summary: Foreign-agent, foreign-influence, special-registry, and similar labeling systems are standing-defective when a public mark tied to funding origin or affiliation does the real work of suspicion, donor deterrence, public delegitimation, or civic thinning instead of a narrow, neutral, evidence-based, and reviewable transparency function.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when financial-service access becomes the practical source of whether association can function
claims.summary: Account freezes, de-banking, payment blocking, payroll interruption, and similar financial-service restrictions are standing-defective when they do the real work of deciding whether lawful association may operate instead of a narrow, evidence-based, reviewable, and time-bounded control tied to concrete wrongdoing.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when compelled civic legibility does the real work of disabling association
claims.summary: Membership lists, donor disclosure, beneficiary identification, staff/controller registries, and comparable record demands are standing-defective when compelled revelation does the real work of chilling, sorting, or disabling lawful association instead of a narrow, privacy-disciplined, reviewable accountability function.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when composite scores become the portable proxy for a person's practical standing
claims.summary: Social scoring, reputation systems, and comparable composite metrics are standing-defective when they do the real work of deciding trust, access, scrutiny, opportunity, or penalty across contexts instead of serving a narrow, purpose-bound, reviewable judgment tied to the specific relation at issue.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when access to or alteration of brain activity becomes a governance path into the person
claims.summary: Neurotechnology, neurodata processing, and brain-directed intervention are standing-defective when they do the real work of steering, screening, persuading, ranking, or burdening persons through thought, attention, emotion, or neural vulnerability instead of serving a tightly bounded, consent-governed, privacy-hardened, medically necessary, and independently reviewable purpose.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when surface-reading systems become administrative title to inward state
claims.summary: Emotion recognition, affect inference, engagement scoring, and comparable surface-reading systems are standing-defective when guessed feeling, sincerity, attitude, or disposition does the real work of discipline, screening, ranking, persuasion, or exclusion instead of a tightly bounded, genuinely protective, low-stakes, and contestable purpose.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when projected future danger becomes a practical title to present suspicion
claims.summary: Predictive policing, hotspot forecasting, and comparable future-risk systems are standing-defective when modelled future offending or dangerousness does the real work of patrol, stop, surveillance, questioning, or restraint instead of a bounded, individualized, reviewable, and conduct-linked judgment.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when biometric traces become an administrative route to protected or sensitive status
claims.summary: Biometric categorisation, sensitive-attribute inference, and comparable body-reading systems are standing-defective when face, voice, gait, iris, fingerprint, or other embodied data do the real work of assigning politically or socially consequential class-membership instead of serving a narrowly bounded, strictly necessary, proportionate, reviewable, and non-discriminatory purpose.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when ambient appearance is turned into searchable face stock for later power
claims.summary: Untargeted face scraping, facial-database manufacture, and comparable stockpiling systems are standing-defective when images from the internet, CCTV, or other ambient sources do the real work of making persons later searchable across contexts instead of serving a narrowly bounded, lawfully acquired, necessary, proportionate, reviewable, and retention-disciplined identification purpose.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when system design obtains compliance by quietly impairing informed and resistible choice
claims.summary: Manipulative AI, deceptive steering, and comparable behaviour-shaping systems are standing-defective when subliminal, purposefully manipulative, deceptive, or vulnerability-exploitative design does the real work of securing purchase, disclosure, attachment, consent, or compliance instead of overt, intelligible, reviewable, and contestable reasons.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when ordinary public passage is made conditionally machine-recognisable through live biometric matching
claims.summary: Real-time remote biometric identification and comparable live biometric searchability in public space are standing-defective when movement, assembly, access, or ordinary presence become contingent on remote machine matchability rather than on a truly exceptional, specifically targeted, lawfully authorised, necessary, proportionate, and reviewable use.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when practical trust depends on a counterfeit person or human counterpart
claims.summary: Synthetic impersonation, deepfakes, cloned voices, and undisclosed AI interaction are standing-defective when another party's trust, disclosure, obedience, accusation, consent, or public judgment depends on believing they are dealing with a real or correctly identified person or human counterpart when they are not, absent clear disclosure, authenticity discipline, contestability, and narrowly bounded justification.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when hooks and difficult disengagement do the real work of securing repeated return and prolonged attention
claims.summary: Addictive design, compulsion engineering, and comparable loop-based systems are standing-defective when streaks, autoplay, rabbit-hole recommenders, rewards for engagement, read-receipt pressure, or friction-heavy exit do the real work of capturing attention, repeated return, disclosure, spending, attachment, or dependence instead of bounded, user-directed, easy-to-stop use.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when interface friction rather than fair reason keeps a person subscribed, paying, disclosed, or locked in
claims.summary: Dark patterns, cancellation traps, and comparable friction-asymmetry systems are standing-defective when signup, assent, disclosure, or payment are made materially easier than refusal, privacy protection, comparison, or cancellation, so that burden asymmetry does the real work of sustaining obligation or extraction instead of clear terms, informed uptake, and reachable exit.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when profile-shaped pricing rather than public terms does the real work of what this person must pay
claims.summary: Surveillance pricing, personalised pricing, and comparable profile-shaped offer systems are standing-defective when personal data, behavioural traces, inferred willingness to pay, urgency, or loyalty dependence do the real work of setting the price, fee, discount, or access term for materially similar goods or services rather than leaving price on public, contestable, and general enough terms.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when tracked managerial automation rather than bounded and contestable human judgment does the real work of setting livelihood terms
claims.summary: Algorithmic management, worker surveillance, and comparable dashboard-governed labor systems are standing-defective when tracked data, opaque metrics, automated assignment, or system-shaped escalation do the real work of setting pace, pay, opportunity, discipline, or retention rather than bounded monitoring, intelligible standards, and genuinely contestable human judgment.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when opaque screening dossiers rather than fair and answerable judgment do the real work of deciding who gets a home and on what terms
claims.summary: Tenant screening, rental blacklists, and comparable housing-access dossiers are standing-defective when eviction records, criminal-history fields, credit files, third-party vendor data, or rental risk scores do the real work of denying housing or imposing burdened housing terms rather than fair relevance limits, maximum possible accuracy, visibility, dispute, non-discrimination, and genuinely answerable human judgment.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when prior-authorization gates and claims mazes rather than clinically answerable judgment do the real work of delaying or denying care
claims.summary: Prior authorization, claims automation, and comparable utilization-management systems are standing-defective when documentation loops, opaque internal criteria, default denial paths, or appeal labor do the real work of determining whether medically necessary care arrives in time rather than leaving care governed by clinical need, specific reasons, bounded timelines, continuity protections, and genuinely answerable human judgment.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when hounding rather than verified and answerable obligation does the real work of extracting payment
claims.summary: Debt collection, contact pressure, and comparable post-transaction extraction systems are standing-defective when repeated calls, inconvenient communication, weak validation, stale-debt threats, or exposure tactics do the real work of getting payment rather than leaving payment governed by validated debt, fair notice, bounded communication, reachable dispute, and answerable process.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when hidden mandatory charges or late-stage total-price revelation do the real work of securing agreement
claims.summary: Junk fees, drip pricing, and comparable price-ambush systems are standing-defective when hidden mandatory charges, staged fee revelation, or preselected paid add-ons do the real work of assent rather than leaving payment governed by clear upfront total price, explicit opt-in for extras, and meaningful comparison or exit.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when practical public voice is governed by opaque moderation, hidden ranking control, or weak redress
claims.summary: Platform moderation, recommender systems, and comparable visibility-control arrangements are standing-defective when explanation-thin moderation, secret demotion, profiling-based recommendation, or contestability-thin review do the real work of deciding who is heard, found, restored, or effectively buried rather than leaving speech standing governed by clear rules, stated reasons, user choice, and reachable redress.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when ordinary opportunity is governed by opaque consumer reports or background files
claims.summary: Consumer reporting, specialty files, and comparable background-dossier systems are standing-defective when hidden or correction-thin reports do the real work of deciding who gets hired, insured, banked, housed, or otherwise allowed to proceed rather than leaving ordinary opportunity governed by visible criteria, specified purpose, adverse-action notice, and reachable correction.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when standing-bearing access is governed by portal competence rather than by the underlying right
claims.summary: Digital-only administration, portal services, and comparable app-first systems are standing-defective when benefits, schooling, complaints, hearings, identification, or other public and essential services are made to depend on help-thin portals, proofing stacks, or device requirements rather than on genuinely accessible digital channels backed by reachable human, proxy, and offline routes.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when child protection or lawful age control is governed by compulsory identification rather than by minimal age proof
claims.summary: Age assurance, age verification, and comparable age-gating systems are standing-defective when full-ID disclosure, retained biometrics or profiling traces, cross-service linkage, or opaque age error do the real work of deciding access rather than proportionate, privacy-preserving, data-minimizing, and contestable proof of only the age fact the setting truly needs.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when movement and sensitive visits are governed by saleable location exhaust rather than by bounded, necessity-tied location use
claims.summary: Location-data brokerage, geofencing, and comparable movement-trace markets are standing-defective when precise visits, routines, or presence at sensitive places are sold, licensed, transferred, or quietly reused so that bought movement data does the real work of exposure, targeting, profiling, or exclusion rather than remaining tied to a narrow operational need that can be publicly answered for.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when learning or assessment is governed by suspicion-heavy monitoring rather than bounded educational purpose
claims.summary: Student monitoring, remote proctoring, classroom-management telemetry, and comparable systems are standing-defective when continuous watching, recording, behavioural flagging, or provider self-use of student data do the real work of trust, discipline, participation, or eligibility rather than remaining tightly tied to bounded educational tasks, minimization, accessible challenge, and answerable human review.

claims.title: righteousness is burdened when ordinary digital participation is governed by surveillance surrender or payment for privacy rather than by a genuinely equivalent less-intrusive alternative
claims.summary: Consent-or-pay models, tracking walls, and comparable access arrangements are standing-defective when behavioural-tracking consent or a fee paid to avoid that tracking does the real work of access rather than leaving users a genuinely equivalent, less-intrusive, and nonpunitive route that does not turn privacy into a premium feature.
